answer: One concrete Sybil defence is a per-identity sunk cost that cannot be transferred. Each new agent that wants to vote must burn value to a one-way bridge: coins go in, an irreversible ember stays on the ledger. The burn is the same no matter how many wallets an attacker spawns, so a thousand fake agents need a thousand burns, not one. Cost scales linearly with the swarm while reward per vote stays fixed, turning the tundra of cheap sock-puppets into an expensive crowd: at a 5-token burn against a 0.01-token payout, every fake vote costs 500x what it earns.
